sections.title: Product foundations
sections.description: What SCI Companion is, what it operates on, and the compatibility boundary readers should assume.

entries.title: SCI Companion overview
entries.summary: A Windows IDE for creating and maintaining Sierra Creative Interpreter games.
what: Provides one desktop workspace for scripts, pictures, views, fonts, audio, messages, vocabularies, and other SCI resources.
Targets game projects from SCI0 through SCI1.1 as the documented support range.
how: Runs as a native MFC multiple-document application built from `SCICompanion.sln`.
Routes most product behavior through `SCICompanionLib`, with resource-specific documents, views, dialogs, compiler code, and storage code.
entries.why: Recorded in D-001: the established Windows/MFC architecture and thin-executable/shared-library split are the system to maintain unless the maintainer explicitly directs a broader rewrite.

entries.title: Game projects and resources
entries.summary: A game project is user-owned source and resource data, not merely an IDE workspace file.
what: Opens an SCI game directory and exposes its scripts and encoded resources through specialized editors.
Can write compiled scripts, patch files, resource maps or volumes, exports, and other project artifacts.
how: Version and storage detection select resource sources and format-specific readers or writers.
`ResourceMap`, resource entities, and MFC documents carry loaded data into editors and back to storage.
entries.why: Inferred from the resource architecture and test fixtures: SCI generations and storage layouts differ enough that version-aware handling must be central, and user projects must be treated as valuable mutable data.

entries.title: Compatibility scope
entries.summary: The documented product range is SCI0 through SCI1.1; narrower claims need direct evidence.
what: Supports the formats and workflows needed for documented SCI0 through SCI1.1 game projects.
Includes recent compatibility fixes for running file dialogs under Wine, without claiming a complete Wine support matrix.
how: SCI version traits and format-specific implementations branch parsing, rendering, compilation, and writing behavior.
Unit fixtures cover representative variants; manual checks cover workflows that native tests do not exercise.
entries.why: The SCI family is not one uniform format. The support statement follows the root README; architecture notes explicitly avoid turning the presence of SCI2 picture fixtures into a claim of full SCI2 support.

sections.title: System architecture
sections.description: The major runtime boundaries and the direction information moves through the native application.

entries.title: Application shell
entries.summary: The `SCICompanion` project starts MFC, restores preferences, and wires document templates to frames and views.
what: Creates the desktop process, main frame, editor document templates, recent-file behavior, and application preferences.
Provides the Windows resources and shipped files that surround the reusable library.
how: `SCICompanionApp::InitInstance()` initializes app state and OLE, selects the `mtnPhilms` registry profile, loads settings, and registers MFC document templates.
Each document template connects a resource document class to its frame and view classes.
entries.why: Recorded in D-001: the executable stays thin so reusable editor, resource, and compiler behavior remains concentrated in `SCICompanionLib`.

entries.title: Shared application library
entries.summary: `SCICompanionLib` owns most domain behavior and editor implementation.
entries.what: Supplies resource storage, compiler/decompiler logic, documents, views, frames, dialogs, utilities, media handling, and shared application state to the executable and tests.
how: Builds as a static MFC library referenced by both the executable and native test projects.
Organizes major areas beneath `SCICompanionLib/Src/`, with `AppState` coordinating cross-cutting application services.
entries.why: Recorded in D-001 and reinforced by the existing project graph: keeping behavior in a shared library lets the shell and tests use the same implementations while preserving the established MFC design.

entries.title: Resource system
entries.summary: Version-aware loaders and writers translate SCI storage into editable resource entities.
what: Enumerates, loads, creates, deletes, and saves typed SCI resources.
Hides resource-map, volume, patch-file, and version-specific details from higher editor layers where possible.
how: Resource sources feed blobs and metadata into `ResourceMap` and resource-specific entity decoders.
Documents and tools modify entities, then encoders and selected resource sources persist the result.
entries.why: Inferred from the component boundaries and tests: centralizing storage/version decisions reduces the chance that each editor implements incompatible file handling and helps protect unrelated game resources during a save.

entries.title: Document/view editors
entries.summary: MFC document, frame, and view classes implement resource-specific editing experiences.
entries.what: Presents pictures, raster assets, scripts, audio, messages, text, vocabularies, and related resources in specialized editors with save and update behavior.
how: `MFCDocuments/` owns editable models and save/undo integration.
`MFCViews/` renders and edits those models, while `MFCFrames/`, `Dialogs/`, and `FrameComponents/` supply windows, commands, and tool panes.
entries.why: Inferred from MFC's document/view model and the registered templates: separating model lifetime from presentation allows several resource editors to share application conventions while retaining format-specific UI.

entries.title: Compiler and language tools
entries.summary: The IDE parses, compiles, inspects, formats, and decompiles SCI scripts.
what: Turns supported script source into game resources and reports diagnostics to the editing workflow.
Supports class browsing, syntax analysis, formatting, decompilation, and version-specific code generation.
how: Parser and syntax-context code create language structures consumed by compile contexts and bytecode/resource generation.
Decompiler paths reconstruct source-like output from compiled scripts; the class browser indexes project definitions.
entries.why: Inferred from the product's role as an IDE: keeping language operations in one subsystem makes editor diagnostics, project compilation, browsing, and tests share the same understanding of supported syntax.

sections.title: Core workflows
sections.description: The main paths a user or maintainer follows through the application.

entries.title: Open and identify a game
entries.summary: Selecting a game directory establishes the active SCI version, resource storage, and project context.
entries.what: Loads a selected existing game so its resources and scripts become available in the explorer and editors.
how: The shell obtains a directory through a persistent file/folder dialog and passes it into application and resource-map state.
Detection logic inspects the game data, chooses SCI traits and resource sources, and populates the explorer.
entries.why: Inferred from the supported format range: detection must precede editing because the same resource type can use different encodings and capabilities across SCI generations.

entries.title: Edit, save, and reload a resource
entries.summary: Resource changes move through an editor document into version-aware persistent storage.
entries.what: Lets a user change a resource, save it into a disposable or backed-up game project, close it, and reopen it with the change preserved.
how: A resource document owns the editable entity and notifies its view as commands mutate state.
Saving encodes the entity for the active SCI version and commits it through the selected resource source; reloading exercises the reader path again.
entries.why: Inferred from user-data risk and the test strategy: save/reload is the meaningful persistence contract, while checking only an in-memory editor state would miss writer and compatibility failures.

entries.title: Compile and run a game
entries.summary: Script compilation updates game resources; run profiles launch the selected interpreter or emulator.
what: Compiles changed scripts and reports errors for navigation and correction.
Launches a configured game executable or interpreter with its stored parameters.
how: Compiler code parses source and headers, resolves symbols and classes, then generates script resources for the active game.
`RunLogic` stores executable profiles and launches the chosen program using the configured path and arguments.
entries.why: Inferred from the IDE workflow: compilation and launch are connected so authors can move quickly from source changes to a game run, while explicit profiles accommodate different interpreters and local installations.

entries.title: Import, export, and convert assets
entries.summary: Dialogs bridge common media formats and SCI-specific resource encodings.
entries.what: Imports or converts images, audio, palettes, and other assets into supported SCI resources and exports resources for external use.
how: Format-specific dialog and resource code decodes the selected input, applies user-selected conversion settings, and creates or updates a resource entity.
Save dialogs choose a resource number, package, and storage path before persistence.
entries.why: Inferred from the dialog and media architecture: conversion needs explicit previews and options because modern source media rarely matches SCI palette, resolution, audio, or encoding limits directly.

sections.title: Maintenance and assurance
sections.description: How contributors build confidence, preserve project memory, and handle risky boundaries.

entries.title: Build environment
entries.summary: The native solution requires Windows, Visual Studio C++/MFC, and a compatible Windows SDK.
entries.what: Builds the Prof-UIS dependency, shared library, executable, and unit-test DLL for the selected solution configuration.
how: Run `msbuild SCICompanion.sln /m /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=Win32` from a compatible Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt.
The checked-in projects mostly request `v140_xp`; one library configuration names `v145`, so the verified modern retargeting recipe remains open work.
entries.why: Recorded in D-001 for the native architecture. The unresolved toolchain detail remains visible as Q-001 and P1-02 rather than being replaced with an unverified compatibility claim.

entries.title: Verification strategy
entries.summary: Documentation checks run everywhere; native tests and workflow checks require a Windows-capable environment.
what: Checks documentation references and the 3x manual source on any system with Python 3.
Uses a Visual Studio native test DLL for covered logic and manual smoke tests for editor workflows and compatibility.
how: `tools/check_docs.py` validates repository-memory documents; `tools/3x_manual.py check` validates triads, evidence presence, and related IDs.
`vstest.console.exe Release\UnitTests.dll` runs the discovered native tests after a successful build; release checks use disposable SCI0 and SCI1.1 projects.
entries.why: Recorded in the testing guide: each check should state both what it proves and what it cannot, because a generated document pass does not prove C++ behavior and native unit tests do not prove complete UI or format compatibility.

entries.title: Preferences and local state
entries.summary: Registry-backed settings remember editor preferences, paths, recent files, and run profiles on the local machine.
entries.what: Persists application and dialog choices between sessions and offers a startup reset path when settings become invalid.
how: MFC profile APIs read and write beneath the `mtnPhilms` application registry key.
Holding Shift during startup follows the current reset path; persistent dialogs separately retain their last folder.
entries.why: Inferred from desktop usability and current implementation: local persistence avoids repeated configuration, while an explicit reset path provides recovery from stale or incompatible settings.

entries.title: Security and data-safety boundaries
entries.summary: Game data, imported media, paths, registry values, and process arguments are untrusted inputs.
entries.what: Protects user projects and the host machine from malformed resources, unsafe process launch, accidental overwrite, and disclosure of private paths or assets.
how: Format handlers validate counts, offsets, sizes, and encodings; contributors add negative cases at changed boundaries.
Tests use committed fixtures or disposable copies, process launch preserves argument boundaries, and reports are sanitized before sharing.
entries.why: Recorded in the security and agent guidance: SCI Companion crosses file-format, filesystem, registry, and process boundaries while operating on valuable user-owned projects, so safe failure and recoverability are part of correctness.

entries.title: Repository memory and the 3x manual
entries.summary: Canonical Markdown carries project truth; this generated manual offers a cross-cutting What/How/Why reading path.
what: Keeps workflow, plans, current state, architecture, decisions, tests, and security guidance in explicitly owned Markdown files.
Generates `docs/manual.html` from this JSON source as a searchable orientation layer.
how: `docs/README.md` assigns one canonical home to each kind of fact and defines update triggers.
`tools/3x_manual.py` validates each manual entry's What/How/Why triad and builds a standalone HTML file; `tools/check_docs.py` validates the canonical Markdown set.
entries.why: Recorded in D-002 and D-003: durable facts should survive individual sessions without being duplicated into drifting tool-specific instructions, while the 3x view makes the same system easier to explore across user behavior, internals, and rationale.
